newsitem.title: POLAND: Suspected killers of Polish ex-prime minister on trial.
newsitem.headline: Suspected killers of Polish ex-prime minister on trial.

text.p: Four men charged with the 1992 murder of a former Polish prime minister and his wife are due to go on trial on Monday, the Warsaw Prosecutor's Office said on Sunday.

"The trial of four men accused of murdering former communist prime minister Piotr Jaroszewicz and his wife Alicja will begin on Monday before the Warsaw Provincial Court," PAP news agency quoted prosecutor's spokesman Ryszard Kucinski as saying.
The accused -- three 54-year-olds and one aged 41 -- are all from the Warsaw area and have pleaded not guilty.
Jaroszewicz, 83, was tortured and strangled in his villa in the Warsaw suburb of Anin, and his wife was shot in the head. Their bodies were discovered the following day by their son.

A commander of the Soviet-controlled Polish army in World War Two, Jaroszewicz served as prime minister during the 1970s under communist party boss Edward Gierek and was widely disliked for his reputation as "Moscow's man in Warsaw".
Initially the crime was believed by some to be politically motivated, but the investigation showed that only material motives were involved.
"The perpetrators did not know the identity of their victims and first learnt it from the media," Kucinski said.
If convicted, the four could face the death penalty, which remains on the books in Poland, although a moratorium on its implementation exists.
